chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): In
a man who gave as charity his share in a house to a man, he said: 'It is valid, even if he did not know what it is.'
ai.seo_question: Is a charity gift valid if the donor doesn't know the exact details of the property being gifted?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the validity of *sadaqah* even in cases of minor uncertainty (*gharar*) regarding the specific share, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that charity is favored and technical defects do not invalidate the act if the donor's intent is clear. It highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding property transactions, prioritizing the spiritual merit of giving over rigid formalism, provided the donor possesses a legitimate, albeit vaguely defined, interest in the asset.
